chapters.1: Daniel and three friends are taken to Babylon as young captives to be trained for royal service. They refuse to eat the king's rich food in order to stay faithful to their beliefs, and God rewards their integrity by making them healthier and wiser than everyone else in the court.
chapters.2: King Nebuchadnezzar has a troubling dream that none of his wise men can interpret because he refuses to tell them what it was. Daniel prays for insight, reveals the dream of a statue made of four different metals representing a succession of world kingdoms, and explains that God will ultimately set up an eternal kingdom that crushes them all.
chapters.3: Nebuchadnezzar sets up a golden statue and commands everyone to worship it, but Daniel's friends Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refuse and are thrown into a blazing furnace. God miraculously protects them so they walk out completely unharmed, leading the king to honor their God.
chapters.4: Nebuchadnezzar has another dream, this time about a great tree that is cut down, which Daniel explains predicts the king's own fall from power due to his pride. The prophecy comes true: Nebuchadnezzar temporarily loses his sanity and kingdom, living like an animal, until he acknowledges God's supreme rule and is restored.
chapters.5: At a drunken feast, King Belshazzar of Babylon disrespects God by using temple vessels for wine, and a mysterious hand writes a message on the wall that no one can read. Daniel interprets it as a sign that Belshazzar's kingdom is about to end, and that very night Babylon falls to the Medes and Persians.
chapters.6: Daniel, now serving under King Darius, is targeted by jealous officials who trick the king into a decree banning prayer to anyone but himself. Daniel keeps praying to God anyway and is thrown into a den of lions, but God protects him and he emerges unharmed, prompting Darius to honor Daniel's God.
chapters.7: Daniel has a vision of four terrifying beasts rising from the sea, representing a succession of powerful kingdoms, followed by a vision of God (the Ancient of Days) in judgment. The vision culminates in a figure called "one like the Son of man" receiving an everlasting kingdom from God that will never be destroyed.
chapters.8: Daniel sees a vision of a ram and a goat locked in fierce battle, representing the clash of the Medo-Persian and Greek empires, followed by the rise of a small but fierce horn that attacks God's people and his sanctuary. An angel explains the vision points to future persecution before an eventual end.
chapters.9: Daniel prays a long prayer of confession on behalf of his people, acknowledging their sin and asking God to restore Jerusalem as promised. The angel Gabriel responds with a detailed prophecy of "seventy weeks" determined for Jerusalem, marking out a timeline leading to the coming and eventual death of an anointed one (the Messiah).
chapters.10: Daniel, in mourning and fasting, receives a vision of a glorious heavenly messenger who tells him that his prayers have been heard, though opposition in the spiritual realm delayed the response. The messenger prepares Daniel to receive a long, detailed prophecy about what is still to come.
chapters.11: This chapter gives a long, detailed prophecy about a series of future kings and conflicts between the "king of the north" and "king of the south," describing wars, alliances, and betrayals affecting God's people over an extended period. It culminates in the rise of an especially arrogant and blasphemous ruler who persecutes the faithful before ultimately coming to his end.
chapters.12: The book closes with a promise that in a time of unprecedented trouble, God's people will be delivered and many of the dead will be raised, some to everlasting life and some to shame. Daniel is told to seal up the vision since its full meaning is for a future time, and is given a blessing for those who wait faithfully to the end.
